title: HTML panels in a real room
blurb: WebXR panels pressed with a tracked fingertip, attached to detected walls and tables with anchors, hidden behind real objects by depth sensing, and shown as an XR quad layer. A simulated room runs the same code without a headset.
question: Can HTML panels use what a WebXR session knows about the room: fingertips, detected walls and tables, anchors, depth and compositor layers?
result: In a simulated room and a headset emulator, fingertip presses, plane snapping and anchors work. Detected planes, depth and quad layers are unverified until the page runs on a device.
